name: Spotify editorial playlists (Spotify for Artists pitch)
instructions: Log in to Spotify for Artists, go to Music > Upcoming and pick the song. Pitch an unreleased song at least 7 days before release: that also gets it onto followers' Release Radar. One song pitched at a time. Once the song is live it can no longer be pitched. You can edit the pitch up to release day, but editors may not see the changes.
notes: Spotify's own route to its editorial playlists. The article says 'pitching doesn't guarantee playlist placement' and editors may pick a different song. It mentions no fee; pitching in Spotify for Artists is free. The release must be delivered via the distributor well ahead of the release date to leave the 7+ days.

name: SubmitHub
instructions: Make an artist account, add the track, choose curators (filter by indie/alt/rock), then send with premium credits (curator must listen 60s+, reply within 72h with approval or 20+ words of feedback, else the credit comes back) or free standard credits (2 every 4 hours; curator may decide without feedback).
notes: Premium credits from $1 each, about $0.80 average in bulk ($80 per 100); curators cost 1-5 credits. Free tier: 2 standard credits every 4 hours, only some curators accept them (https://www.submithub.com/help/QPHgFWDSCm82W7vLJ). SubmitHub says you pay for curators' time, not placement, and you can't pay extra to be shared. Several rows in spotify-uk/world already route via SubmitHub.

name: Groover
instructions: Sign up as an artist, upload or link the track, pick curators (playlists, blogs, radio, labels) by genre, and pay in Grooviz. Curators have 7 days to reply.
notes: 2 Grooviz (EUR 2) per standard curator, 4-6 for some top curators; 1 Grooviz = EUR 1 incl. tax; packs from EUR 47 with up to 20% off. No reply in 7 days = Grooviz refunded. Average answer rate over 85% (per Groover). Several rows in spotify-uk already route via Groover curator profiles.

name: Musosoup
instructions: Submit a link or MP3 for free. Musosoup checks it is ready for coverage (up to 24h). If accepted, pay the campaign fee to go live. Curators (blogs, playlists, radio, influencers) then send offers, and you choose which to accept. A campaign can be set up up to 90 days before release.
notes: UK platform. GBP 42 campaign fee, paid only once accepted, refunded if there is no coverage at all. Spotify playlisting is included free ('Free Spotify playlisting and social shares'). Other paid curator offers are set by curators, averaging GBP 8-12, and always come with a free option.

name: Soundplate playlist submissions (play.soundplate.com)
instructions: Pick a relevant playlist from the grid and submit the track to that curator's form. Only submit to playlists that fit, and don't spam.
notes: A free service from Soundplate Records connecting artists with independent Spotify and Deezer curators. Several indie playlists in spotify-uk.json already use it (e.g. play.soundplate.com/newudiuk, /indie406). Soundplate's own 'Best New Indie' link (play.soundplate.com/bni) listed at soundplate.com/submit-music returned 404, so no row for it.

name: SubmitLink
instructions: Paste the Spotify track link, pick playlists (by hand or from AI suggestions) and send a campaign. Paid: $2-5 per playlist. Free: one song to two playlists every 24 hours (only curators who accept free submissions).
notes: Spotify-only, released tracks only. No guaranteed placement or streams (FAQ). No reply in 7 days = credit back as SubmitLink credit, not a card refund. Screens playlists with artist.tools data; the homepage's 'guaranteed bot-free' is stronger than the FAQ's wording. Newer than SubmitHub/Groover.

name: Daily Playlists
instructions: Make an account and submit the song through the free Standard tier, which reaches a marketplace of 18,000+ playlists. Premium credits send it to vetted curators with faster, guaranteed responses.
notes: Free tier is 'Free Forever' with 10 submissions a week. Professional is $19.99/month ($199.99/year) for 30 weekly standard submissions plus analysis. The premium credit price isn't on the pricing page. Many of the playlists are small, so check each one's followers and activity before relying on it.

name: Playlist Push
instructions: Apply as an artist, set the track's genres, moods and language ('Playlist DNA'), choose a budget in the Campaign Calculator, and the track goes to matching independent Spotify curators for paid review.
notes: Spotify campaigns have a $280 minimum (e.g. $630 reached 79 playlists). You pay for curator review, with no guaranteed adds or streams, and the Artist Protection Fund credits back reviews that don't happen. Too expensive for a first indie band campaign; SubmitHub or Groover reach similar curators per pound. Not available in some regions.

name: alexrainbirdMusic (YouTube channel and playlists)
instructions: Submit through the SubmitHub link on the channel's About page: $3 for no feedback, $5 with feedback (full listen, reply within 3 days, refund if missed). The About page also lists a District portal, https://alexrainbirdmusic.portal.district.biz/. alexrainbirdmusic@gmail.com is for other enquiries only, not submissions.
notes: UK couple (Alex and Beth Rainbird) curating indie, pop, folk and rock since 2011. SubmitHub page: '1.4 million YT subs, 140k Spotify followers'; individual playlists have about 1k-22k followers. Leans acoustic and indie-folk, so pitch the softer tracks. followers left null because the channel count came from the SubmitHub page, not a playlist page.
